$comment: The one-rule TextMate INJECTION grammar for para/db's `@sql { … }` expression tier — it highlights an `@sql` body as SQL in VS Code. This is the whole editor-highlighting mechanism for a third-party tier, documented in the Noeta extension README (Text tiers section): a package ships a grammar of this shape targeting `L:source.noeta`; it needs NO change to Noeta's own static grammar (which stays fixed) and no cooperation from the core extension. Install it by contributing it from any VS Code extension's `grammars` with `injectTo: ["source.noeta"]` and `embeddedLanguages: { "meta.embedded.block.sql": "sql" }` — see this package's README. Brace counting mirrors the compiler lexer's matching_brace (nested pairs recurse; `\{` `\}` `\\` are literal), so a `{…}` in the SQL never ends the block. `${…}` holes scope back to source.noeta, so a hole highlights as ordinary Noeta inside the SQL — the same split the compiler makes (statics = SQL text, holes = checked Noeta expressions).

tier-escape.$comment: The text-body escapes \{ \} \\ plus \$ (a literal $ that would otherwise open a hole) — matched first so an escaped closer or dollar never triggers a rule below.
tier-escape.name: constant.character.escape.noeta

tier-hole.$comment: A `${ … }` hole is an ordinary Noeta expression — scope its contents back to source.noeta so it highlights as code, not SQL.

tier-brace-pair.$comment: A nested balanced brace pair inside the SQL body — recursion is how TextMate counts depth, so a `{…}` in the text does not close the block.
